sentences.text: 2. On being served with notice of revision petition, respondent nos.1 and 5 entered appearance, but they chose not to file reply to revision petition.

3. The brief factual matrix of the case is that complainant/respondent no.2 Reena gave a complaint dated 11.06.2015 in CAW Cell Krishna Nagar, mentioning therein allegations of demand of dowry and cruelty, criminal breach of trust in respect of istridhan and criminal intimidation by the accused persons, including the revisionist;
O n t h e b a s i s o f s a i d c o m p l a i n t , F I R N o . 1 1 7 / 2 0 1 6 u n d e r S e c t i o n s 498A/406/506(II)/34 IPC was registered against the accused persons and vide impugned order dated 06.02.2023, charges under Sections 498A/406/506(II)/34 IPC were ordered to be framed against the accused persons.
Charges were framed on the same day.
Being aggrieved with framing of charges, the revisionist, who is Nanad of the complainant, has preferred the instant revision petition.
4. None has appeared on behalf of revisionist to argue the present revision petition.
Liberty was given to revisionist to file written arguments and same has been filed on 14.08.2023.

In the body of revision petition as well as in written submissions filed on behalf of revisionist, it is submitted that there are general and omnibus allegations against the revisionist in the FIR, name of revisionist cropped up in the complaint only with names of other Crl.

(R) 103/23 :: 3 ::
accused persons; no specific or distinct allegations have been made against her; no allegations under Sections 498A, 406 and 506(II) IPC are imputed to the revisionist,
therefore, the revisionist should not have been charged for the offences mentioned in charges and impugned order is liable to be set aside.

Reliance has been placed on the following judgments: (1) Geeta Mehrotra vs. State of UP, 2012, 10 SC 740 and (2)
Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Ors [Crl. Appeal No.
195/2022, decided by Hon'ble Apex Court on 08.02.2022].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In both these judgments,
it has been held that on the basis of general and omnibus allegations against the family members of husband, it would be unjust to force them to go through the tribulations of a trial.

5. On the other hand, Ld. Addl PP and Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2 have argued that there is sufficient material available on record against the accused persons including the revisionist and they have been rightly charged.
There is no illegality or impropriety in the impugned order and revision petition deserves dismissal.
6. I have heard Addl PP for the State, Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2 and considered written submissions filed on behalf of revisionist and material available on record.
7. Complaint dated 11.06.2015 given in CAW Cell is genesis of present case, on the basis of which present FIR was registered.
This complaint is against husband and his family members including the revisionist Sunita, who is Nanad of the complainant.

This complaint mentions that her father-in-law, Crl. (R) 103/23 :: 4 ::

2 mother-in-law, two sisters-in-law (nanad), namely, Sunita (revisionist herein) and Manju were also residing with her husband.

After completion of post marriage ceremonies, her husband and mother-in-law asked her to hand over all ornaments to keep them safe and she entrusted the ornaments to her husband and mother-in-law and thereafter they did not return ornaments.
She further stated that all her istridhan articles and dowry articles are with her husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law.

8. In the aforesaid complaint, the complainant further mentions that behaviour of her husband,
father-in-law, mother-in- law and her Nanads has been insulting towards her since beginning; they used to taunt her and demand more money and car.
When the complainant stated that said demand cannot be fulfilled, she was given beating by her husband and family members, including her Nanads.

On 20.04.2005, her husband had beaten her and when she tried to run out of the house to save her, Sunita (revisionist herein) and Manju caught her and bolted the door and she was given beating by her husband, his parents and sisters.
Her Nanads Sunita and Manju used to abuse and beat her.
9. From the above allegations, it is clear that complainant has not entrusted any dowry or istridhan articles to the revisionist.

Even there are no allegation that revisionist ever extended any threat to life to the complainant, however, allegations of cruelty and harassment on account of demand of dowry are certainly imputed to all the family members including the revisionist.

There are instances mentioned in complaint of torture, where Crl. (R) 103/23 :: 5 ::
revisionist has been specifically named.
Therefore, no case for charge under Section 406/506(II) IPC is made out against the revisionist and she should not have been charged for the said offences.
Only offence under section 498A IPC for charge is made out against the revisionist.
Considering the same, impugned order to the extent of framing charge against the revisionist under sections 406/506(II) IPC is hereby set aside.
It is held that only a case for charge under section 498A IPC is made out against revisionist.
In view thereof, revision petition stands partly allowed.
10. Trial Court record be sent back along with copy of this order.
File be consigned to Record Room.
